eportal_cooling_permits.description: IMDC VA1 CHILLER ADDITON

power.note: VADEQ air permit 74112 covers this site with 370.2 MW of permitted backup generator capacity across 8 building(s). This building's 8% floor-area share x ICPRB Equation 6-3 (capacity x 0.5 redundancy x 0.8 utilization) = 12.0 MW effective IT load. Floor area is used only to apportion a measured site total, not to generate it -- the 8,818 sqft/MW density bridge is not used for this building.

operator_cross_check.note: interconnection.fyi lists 100-250 MW across IRON MOUNTAIN's Prince William / Manassas portfolio. The floor-area-derived estimate falls outside that span; the operator figure is portfolio-wide rather than building-specific, so it is reported as a flag rather than used to widen the range.

scope1_onsite_cooling.methodology: Effective IT power (MW) x measured Water Use per Unit of Power (150-1577 gal/MW/day). WUP values are ICPRB's, derived from utility-reported data center water use divided by effective power demand in the Loudoun Water, Fairfax Water, and Prince William Water service areas (ICPRB 2025 WMA Water Supply Study, Section 6.2 / Table 6-5). Central estimate uses the Prince William Water observed fleet average of 309 gal/MW/day.
scope1_onsite_cooling.note: Peak-day demand in Prince William Water's service area runs about 10x the annual average (3060 gal/MW/day observed), so summer stress is far higher than the annual figure implies. A consumptive-use factor of 0.75 applies to the delivered volume.

scope2_electricity.methodology: Effective IT MW x PUE (1.3-1.55, standard vintage) x 24 h/day x 198 gal/MWh (Dominion generation-mix-blended consumption factor) = consumptive water at the generating plant. Dominion's 2025 mix is 58% gas / 25% nuclear / 14% renewable / 3% coal. Per-technology factors are VIRGINIA-SPECIFIC, generation-weighted from USGS plant-level model estimates (2015 release v1.2, July 2024) rather than national medians -- nuclear is 242 gal/MWh here against a national median of 700, because Surry discharges to a tidal estuary and consumes nothing while North Anna evaporates from Lake Anna.
scope2_electricity.note: System-average grid intensity, not marginal-generator attribution -- no published marginal water-intensity dataset exists for PJM/Dominion (NREL Cambium is carbon-only).

scope3_embodied.methodology: 5%-15% of the operational (Scope 1 + Scope 2) total, anchored to corporate embodied-vs-operational water disclosure ratios (Privette et al. 2026) -- not a physical estimate specific to this facility's hardware or construction supply chain, which lies entirely outside any Virginia dataset.
scope3_embodied.note: At least one hyperscale operator has disclosed embodied/supply-chain water exceeding 99% of its total corporate water footprint (Privette et al., AGU Advances, 2026) -- that figure reflects a company-wide accounting boundary choice, not a physical per-facility ratio. It is flagged as evidence the 5-15% anchor is a floor, not a ceiling.

scope_water_footprint.total_basis_note: total_mgd_central mixes bases: Scope 1 is DELIVERED water (ICPRB's WUP figures are utility billing records, so blowdown returning to the basin is included), while Scope 2 is CONSUMPTION at the generating plant. total_consumptive_mgd_central puts all three on a consumption basis by applying ICPRB's 0.75 consumptive-use factor to Scope 1. Use the delivered figure against utility supply and the consumptive figure against basin water balance.
scope_water_footprint.total_note: Envelope sum of independent scope minima and maxima -- a conservative bound, not a statistical confidence interval (the three scopes are not assumed to co-vary). The central estimate uses Prince William Water's own observed intensity and is the figure to quote.

benchmark.verdict: Direct on-site estimate (0.004 MGD) is below the water use of an average large office building (0.018 MGD) -- consistent with JLARC's finding that most data centers use no more water than one.

scope1_onsite_cooling.methodology: Effective IT power (MW) x measured Water Use per Unit of Power (150-1577 gal/MW/day). WUP values are ICPRB's, derived from utility-reported data center water use divided by effective power demand in the Loudoun Water, Fairfax Water, and Prince William Water service areas (ICPRB 2025 WMA Water Supply Study, Section 6.2 / Table 6-5). Central estimate uses the Prince William Water observed fleet average of 309 gal/MW/day.
scope1_onsite_cooling.note: Peak-day demand in Prince William Water's service area runs about 10x the annual average (3060 gal/MW/day observed), so summer stress is far higher than the annual figure implies. A consumptive-use factor of 0.75 applies to the delivered volume.

scope2_electricity.methodology: Effective IT MW x PUE (1.3-1.55, standard vintage) x 24 h/day x 198 gal/MWh (Dominion generation-mix-blended consumption factor) = consumptive water at the generating plant. Dominion's 2025 mix is 58% gas / 25% nuclear / 14% renewable / 3% coal. Per-technology factors are VIRGINIA-SPECIFIC, generation-weighted from USGS plant-level model estimates (2015 release v1.2, July 2024) rather than national medians -- nuclear is 242 gal/MWh here against a national median of 700, because Surry discharges to a tidal estuary and consumes nothing while North Anna evaporates from Lake Anna.
scope2_electricity.note: System-average grid intensity, not marginal-generator attribution -- no published marginal water-intensity dataset exists for PJM/Dominion (NREL Cambium is carbon-only).

scope3_embodied.methodology: 5%-15% of the operational (Scope 1 + Scope 2) total, anchored to corporate embodied-vs-operational water disclosure ratios (Privette et al. 2026) -- not a physical estimate specific to this facility's hardware or construction supply chain, which lies entirely outside any Virginia dataset.
scope3_embodied.note: At least one hyperscale operator has disclosed embodied/supply-chain water exceeding 99% of its total corporate water footprint (Privette et al., AGU Advances, 2026) -- that figure reflects a company-wide accounting boundary choice, not a physical per-facility ratio. It is flagged as evidence the 5-15% anchor is a floor, not a ceiling.

scope_water_footprint.total_basis_note: total_mgd_central mixes bases: Scope 1 is DELIVERED water (ICPRB's WUP figures are utility billing records, so blowdown returning to the basin is included), while Scope 2 is CONSUMPTION at the generating plant. total_consumptive_mgd_central puts all three on a consumption basis by applying ICPRB's 0.75 consumptive-use factor to Scope 1. Use the delivered figure against utility supply and the consumptive figure against basin water balance.
scope_water_footprint.total_note: Envelope sum of independent scope minima and maxima -- a conservative bound, not a statistical confidence interval (the three scopes are not assumed to co-vary). The central estimate uses Prince William Water's own observed intensity and is the figure to quote.

scope_water_footprint.total_note: Envelope sum of independent scope minima and maxima -- a conservative bound, not a statistical confidence interval (the three scopes are not assumed to co-vary). The central estimate uses Prince William Water's own observed intensity and is the figure to quote.

benchmark.verdict: Direct on-site estimate (0.004 MGD) is below the water use of an average large office building (0.018 MGD) -- consistent with JLARC's finding that most data centers use no more water than one.

power.note: VADEQ air permit 73741 covers this site with 88.8 MW of permitted backup generator capacity across 3 building(s). scope1_onsite_cooling.narrowed_by: AMAZON: Amazon/AWS reports deploying closed-loop, direct-to-chip cold-plate cooling that adds no evaporative water on new AI infrastructure, and a 42% year-over-year water reduction in its Northern Virginia region (2025 sustainability reporting). Global fleet WUE 0.12 L/kWh.
scope1_onsite_cooling.methodology: Effective IT power (MW) x measured Water Use per Unit of Power (150-309 gal/MW/day). WUP values are ICPRB's, derived from utility-reported data center water use divided by effective power demand in the Loudoun Water, Fairfax Water, and Prince William Water service areas (ICPRB 2025 WMA Water Supply Study, Section 6.2 / Table 6-5). Central estimate uses the Prince William Water observed fleet average of 309 gal/MW/day.
scope1_onsite_cooling.note: Peak-day demand in Prince William Water's service area runs about 10x the annual average (3060 gal/MW/day observed), so summer stress is far higher than the annual figure implies. A consumptive-use factor of 0.75 applies to the delivered volume.

market_based.caveat: Contractual, not physical. Annual REC/PPA matching does not change which plant served this building at 3pm in August, and the water consumed there was consumed there. Reported because the GHG Protocol requires dual reporting and operators quote this figure; the location-based value above is the one that corresponds to water actually leaving a Virginia basin.

scope2_electricity.methodology: Effective IT MW x PUE (1.08-1.2, AWS 2025 global average PUE 1.14 (1.15 in 2024)) x 24 h/day x 198 gal/MWh (Dominion generation-mix-blended consumption factor) = consumptive water at the generating plant. Dominion's 2025 mix is 58% gas / 25% nuclear / 14% renewable / 3% coal. Per-technology factors are VIRGINIA-SPECIFIC, generation-weighted from USGS plant-level model estimates (2015 release v1.2, July 2024) rather than national medians -- nuclear is 242 gal/MWh here against a national median of 700, because Surry discharges to a tidal estuary and consumes nothing while North Anna evaporates from Lake Anna.
scope2_electricity.note: System-average grid intensity, not marginal-generator attribution -- no published marginal water-intensity dataset exists for PJM/Dominion (NREL Cambium is carbon-only).

scope3_embodied.methodology: 5%-15% of the operational (Scope 1 + Scope 2) total, anchored to corporate embodied-vs-operational water disclosure ratios (Privette et al. 2026) -- not a physical estimate specific to this facility's hardware or construction supply chain, which lies entirely outside any Virginia dataset.
scope3_embodied.note: At least one hyperscale operator has disclosed embodied/supply-chain water exceeding 99% of its total corporate water footprint (Privette et al., AGU Advances, 2026) -- that figure reflects a company-wide accounting boundary choice, not a physical per-facility ratio. It is flagged as evidence the 5-15% anchor is a floor, not a ceiling.

scope1_onsite_cooling.narrowed_by: AMAZON: Amazon/AWS reports deploying closed-loop, direct-to-chip cold-plate cooling that adds no evaporative water on new AI infrastructure, and a 42% year-over-year water reduction in its Northern Virginia region (2025 sustainability reporting). Global fleet WUE 0.12 L/kWh.
scope1_onsite_cooling.methodology: Effective IT power (MW) x measured Water Use per Unit of Power (150-309 gal/MW/day). WUP values are ICPRB's, derived from utility-reported data center water use divided by effective power demand in the Loudoun Water, Fairfax Water, and Prince William Water service areas (ICPRB 2025 WMA Water Supply Study, Section 6.2 / Table 6-5). Central estimate uses the Prince William Water observed fleet average of 309 gal/MW/day.
scope1_onsite_cooling.note: Peak-day demand in Prince William Water's service area runs about 10x the annual average (3060 gal/MW/day observed), so summer stress is far higher than the annual figure implies. A consumptive-use factor of 0.75 applies to the delivered volume.

market_based.caveat: Contractual, not physical. Annual REC/PPA matching does not change which plant served this building at 3pm in August, and the water consumed there was consumed there. Reported because the GHG Protocol requires dual reporting and operators quote this figure; the location-based value above is the one that corresponds to water actually leaving a Virginia basin.

scope2_electricity.methodology: Effective IT MW x PUE (1.08-1.2, AWS 2025 global average PUE 1.14 (1.15 in 2024)) x 24 h/day x 198 gal/MWh (Dominion generation-mix-blended consumption factor) = consumptive water at the generating plant. Dominion's 2025 mix is 58% gas / 25% nuclear / 14% renewable / 3% coal. Per-technology factors are VIRGINIA-SPECIFIC, generation-weighted from USGS plant-level model estimates (2015 release v1.2, July 2024) rather than national medians -- nuclear is 242 gal/MWh here against a national median of 700, because Surry discharges to a tidal estuary and consumes nothing while North Anna evaporates from Lake Anna.
scope2_electricity.note: System-average grid intensity, not marginal-generator attribution -- no published marginal water-intensity dataset exists for PJM/Dominion (NREL Cambium is carbon-only).

scope3_embodied.methodology: 5%-15% of the operational (Scope 1 + Scope 2) total, anchored to corporate embodied-vs-operational water disclosure ratios (Privette et al. 2026) -- not a physical estimate specific to this facility's hardware or construction supply chain, which lies entirely outside any Virginia dataset.
scope3_embodied.note: At least one hyperscale operator has disclosed embodied/supply-chain water exceeding 99% of its total corporate water footprint (Privette et al., AGU Advances, 2026) -- that figure reflects a company-wide accounting boundary choice, not a physical per-facility ratio. It is flagged as evidence the 5-15% anchor is a floor, not a ceiling.

scope_water_footprint.total_basis_note: total_mgd_central mixes bases: Scope 1 is DELIVERED water (ICPRB's WUP figures are utility billing records, so blowdown returning to the basin is included), while Scope 2 is CONSUMPTION at the generating plant. total_consumptive_mgd_central puts all three on a consumption basis by applying ICPRB's 0.75 consumptive-use factor to Scope 1. Use the delivered figure against utility supply and the consumptive figure against basin water balance.
scope_water_footprint.total_note: Envelope sum of independent scope minima and maxima -- a conservative bound, not a statistical confidence interval (the three scopes are not assumed to co-vary). The central estimate uses Prince William Water's own observed intensity and is the figure to quote.

benchmark.verdict: Direct on-site estimate (0.003 MGD) is below the water use of an average large office building (0.018 MGD) -- consistent with JLARC's finding that most data centers use no more water than one.

power.note: VADEQ air permit 74052 covers this site with 185.8 MW of permitted backup generator capacity across 4 building(s). scope1_onsite_cooling.narrowed_by: AMAZON: Amazon/AWS reports deploying closed-loop, direct-to-chip cold-plate cooling that adds no evaporative water on new AI infrastructure, and a 42% year-over-year water reduction in its Northern Virginia region (2025 sustainability reporting). Global fleet WUE 0.12 L/kWh.
scope1_onsite_cooling.methodology: Effective IT power (MW) x measured Water Use per Unit of Power (150-309 gal/MW/day). WUP values are ICPRB's, derived from utility-reported data center water use divided by effective power demand in the Loudoun Water, Fairfax Water, and Prince William Water service areas (ICPRB 2025 WMA Water Supply Study, Section 6.2 / Table 6-5). Central estimate uses the Prince William Water observed fleet average of 309 gal/MW/day.
scope1_onsite_cooling.note: Peak-day demand in Prince William Water's service area runs about 10x the annual average (3060 gal/MW/day observed), so summer stress is far higher than the annual figure implies. A consumptive-use factor of 0.75 applies to the delivered volume.

market_based.caveat: Contractual, not physical. Annual REC/PPA matching does not change which plant served this building at 3pm in August, and the water consumed there was consumed there. Reported because the GHG Protocol requires dual reporting and operators quote this figure; the location-based value above is the one that corresponds to water actually leaving a Virginia basin.

scope2_electricity.methodology: Effective IT MW x PUE (1.08-1.2, AWS 2025 global average PUE 1.14 (1.15 in 2024)) x 24 h/day x 198 gal/MWh (Dominion generation-mix-blended consumption factor) = consumptive water at the generating plant. Dominion's 2025 mix is 58% gas / 25% nuclear / 14% renewable / 3% coal. Per-technology factors are VIRGINIA-SPECIFIC, generation-weighted from USGS plant-level model estimates (2015 release v1.2, July 2024) rather than national medians -- nuclear is 242 gal/MWh here against a national median of 700, because Surry discharges to a tidal estuary and consumes nothing while North Anna evaporates from Lake Anna.
scope2_electricity.note: System-average grid intensity, not marginal-generator attribution -- no published marginal water-intensity dataset exists for PJM/Dominion (NREL Cambium is carbon-only).

scope3_embodied.methodology: 5%-15% of the operational (Scope 1 + Scope 2) total, anchored to corporate embodied-vs-operational water disclosure ratios (Privette et al. 2026) -- not a physical estimate specific to this facility's hardware or construction supply chain, which lies entirely outside any Virginia dataset.
scope3_embodied.note: At least one hyperscale operator has disclosed embodied/supply-chain water exceeding 99% of its total corporate water footprint (Privette et al., AGU Advances, 2026) -- that figure reflects a company-wide accounting boundary choice, not a physical per-facility ratio. It is flagged as evidence the 5-15% anchor is a floor, not a ceiling.

scope_water_footprint.total_basis_note: total_mgd_central mixes bases: Scope 1 is DELIVERED water (ICPRB's WUP figures are utility billing records, so blowdown returning to the basin is included), while Scope 2 is CONSUMPTION at the generating plant. total_consumptive_mgd_central puts all three on a consumption basis by applying ICPRB's 0.75 consumptive-use factor to Scope 1. Use the delivered figure against utility supply and the consumptive figure against basin water balance.
scope_water_footprint.total_note: Envelope sum of independent scope minima and maxima -- a conservative bound, not a statistical confidence interval (the three scopes are not assumed to co-vary). The central estimate uses Prince William Water's own observed intensity and is the figure to quote.

benchmark.verdict: Direct on-site estimate (0.004 MGD) is below the water use of an average large office building (0.018 MGD) -- consistent with JLARC's finding that most data centers use no more water than one.

Central estimate uses the Prince William Water observed fleet average of 309 gal/MW/day.
scope1_onsite_cooling.note: Peak-day demand in Prince William Water's service area runs about 10x the annual average (3060 gal/MW/day observed), so summer stress is far higher than the annual figure implies. A consumptive-use factor of 0.75 applies to the delivered volume.

scope2_electricity.methodology: Effective IT MW x PUE (1.15-1.35, new_build vintage) x 24 h/day x 198 gal/MWh (Dominion generation-mix-blended consumption factor) = consumptive water at the generating plant. Dominion's 2025 mix is 58% gas / 25% nuclear / 14% renewable / 3% coal. Per-technology factors are VIRGINIA-SPECIFIC, generation-weighted from USGS plant-level model estimates (2015 release v1.2, July 2024) rather than national medians -- nuclear is 242 gal/MWh here against a national median of 700, because Surry discharges to a tidal estuary and consumes nothing while North Anna evaporates from Lake Anna.
scope2_electricity.note: System-average grid intensity, not marginal-generator attribution -- no published marginal water-intensity dataset exists for PJM/Dominion (NREL Cambium is carbon-only).

scope3_embodied.methodology: 5%-15% of the operational (Scope 1 + Scope 2) total, anchored to corporate embodied-vs-operational water disclosure ratios (Privette et al. 2026) -- not a physical estimate specific to this facility's hardware or construction supply chain, which lies entirely outside any Virginia dataset.
scope3_embodied.note: At least one hyperscale operator has disclosed embodied/supply-chain water exceeding 99% of its total corporate water footprint (Privette et al., AGU Advances, 2026) -- that figure reflects a company-wide accounting boundary choice, not a physical per-facility ratio. It is flagged as evidence the 5-15% anchor is a floor, not a ceiling.

scope_water_footprint.total_basis_note: total_mgd_central mixes bases: Scope 1 is DELIVERED water (ICPRB's WUP figures are utility billing records, so blowdown returning to the basin is included), while Scope 2 is CONSUMPTION at the generating plant. total_consumptive_mgd_central puts all three on a consumption basis by applying ICPRB's 0.75 consumptive-use factor to Scope 1. Use the delivered figure against utility supply and the consumptive figure against basin water balance.
scope_water_footprint.total_note: Envelope sum of independent scope minima and maxima -- a conservative bound, not a statistical confidence interval (the three scopes are not assumed to co-vary). The central estimate uses Prince William Water's own observed intensity and is the figure to quote.

benchmark.verdict: Direct on-site estimate (0.002 MGD) is below the water use of an average large office building (0.018 MGD) -- consistent with JLARC's finding that most data centers use no more water than one.

WUP values are ICPRB's, derived from utility-reported data center water use divided by effective power demand in the Loudoun Water, Fairfax Water, and Prince William Water service areas (ICPRB 2025 WMA Water Supply Study, Section 6.2 / Table 6-5). Central estimate uses the Prince William Water observed fleet average of 309 gal/MW/day.
scope1_onsite_cooling.note: Peak-day demand in Prince William Water's service area runs about 10x the annual average (3060 gal/MW/day observed), so summer stress is far higher than the annual figure implies. A consumptive-use factor of 0.75 applies to the delivered volume.

scope2_electricity.methodology: Effective IT MW x PUE (1.15-1.35, new_build vintage) x 24 h/day x 198 gal/MWh (Dominion generation-mix-blended consumption factor) = consumptive water at the generating plant. Dominion's 2025 mix is 58% gas / 25% nuclear / 14% renewable / 3% coal. Per-technology factors are VIRGINIA-SPECIFIC, generation-weighted from USGS plant-level model estimates (2015 release v1.2, July 2024) rather than national medians -- nuclear is 242 gal/MWh here against a national median of 700, because Surry discharges to a tidal estuary and consumes nothing while North Anna evaporates from Lake Anna.
scope2_electricity.note: System-average grid intensity, not marginal-generator attribution -- no published marginal water-intensity dataset exists for PJM/Dominion (NREL Cambium is carbon-only).

scope3_embodied.methodology: 5%-15% of the operational (Scope 1 + Scope 2) total, anchored to corporate embodied-vs-operational water disclosure ratios (Privette et al. 2026) -- not a physical estimate specific to this facility's hardware or construction supply chain, which lies entirely outside any Virginia dataset.
scope3_embodied.note: At least one hyperscale operator has disclosed embodied/supply-chain water exceeding 99% of its total corporate water footprint (Privette et al., AGU Advances, 2026) -- that figure reflects a company-wide accounting boundary choice, not a physical per-facility ratio. It is flagged as evidence the 5-15% anchor is a floor, not a ceiling.

scope_water_footprint.total_basis_note: total_mgd_central mixes bases: Scope 1 is DELIVERED water (ICPRB's WUP figures are utility billing records, so blowdown returning to the basin is included), while Scope 2 is CONSUMPTION at the generating plant. total_consumptive_mgd_central puts all three on a consumption basis by applying ICPRB's 0.75 consumptive-use factor to Scope 1. Use the delivered figure against utility supply and the consumptive figure against basin water balance.
scope_water_footprint.total_note: Envelope sum of independent scope minima and maxima -- a conservative bound, not a statistical confidence interval (the three scopes are not assumed to co-vary). The central estimate uses Prince William Water's own observed intensity and is the figure to quote.

benchmark.verdict: Direct on-site estimate (0.068 MGD) sits in the normal measured band for Virginia data centers (JLARC 2024).
